deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is the second half of a table of contents ('Inhalt') for Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. It is written in H. Weber's hand (pencil note: 'Handschrift von H. Weber'). The previous page carries Weber's footnote saying the summary comes almost entirely from Riemann. It covers Articles 13–22, in modern terms:

Art.13: Isolated singularities of a holomorphic function w(z) at an interior point.

Art.14: The results of Arts.12–13 applied to interior points of an arbitrary (possibly multi-sheeted, branched) plane surface, using local uniformizing parameters at branch points.

Art.15: General properties of the map from a surface T spread over the z-plane A to a surface S spread over the w-plane B, given by w = f(z). These include conformality away from critical points and branch behaviour.

Art.16 (Dirichlet principle). Fix α+iβ on T and set
Ω(α) = ∫_T [(α_x − β_y)^2 + (α_y + β_x)^2] dT.
Vary α by λ, where λ is continuous (or discontinuous only at isolated points) and λ = 0 on ∂T. Claim: Ω attains a minimum for some λ. Excluding discontinuities removable by changing values at single points, the minimizer is unique.
- [My filling-in] The Euler–Lagrange equation: Ω(α+λ+εh) has ε-derivative −2∫h[∂x(u_x − β_y) + ∂y(u_y + β_x)] dT, with u = α+λ. Since β_yx − β_xy = 0, this reduces to Δu = 0.
- So the minimizer u is harmonic with boundary values α|∂T.
- [My filling-in] The integrand equals |∇α|^2 + |∇β|^2 − 2(α_xβ_y − α_yβ_x). The Jacobian term is a divergence, so for fixed β it is a boundary term unaffected by λ.
- Uniqueness follows from strict convexity of the quadratic functional.

Art.17: Justification, by a limit argument ('Grenzmethode'), of a lemma assumed in Art.16.

Art.18: Let T be connected, cut into a simply connected T* by cross-cuts (Querschnitte), and let α+iβ have finite Ω. Then α+iβ can be turned into a holomorphic function of z in exactly one way by adding μ+iν, where:
(1) μ = 0 on ∂T, and ν is prescribed at one point;
(2) μ (on T) and ν (on T*) are discontinuous only at isolated points, with finite Dirichlet integrals ∫|∇μ|^2 and ∫|∇ν|^2;
(3) the variations of ν agree on both sides of each cross-cut, so ν may jump by constants (periods).
[My filling-in] Here μ = λ from Art.16, and ν is obtained by integrating the conjugate differential −u_y dx + u_x dy − dβ on T*.

Art.19: Survey of necessary and sufficient data determining a holomorphic function on a given domain: boundary values of the real part, singularities, periods.

Art.20: Earlier definitions of functions by analytic expressions contained superfluous data. The present approach reduces the determining data to what is necessary.

Art.21 (Riemann mapping theorem). Two simply connected plane surfaces can always be mapped onto each other continuously and conformally in their smallest parts. The image of one interior point and one boundary point may be prescribed arbitrarily, and this fixes the map completely.

Art.22: Concluding remarks.
errors: No computational errors; the page contains only statements.

Arts.16–18 rest on the existence of a minimizer of the Dirichlet integral. This is assumed, not proved (Art.17 only treats a subsidiary lemma). Weierstrass criticized it (1870); Hilbert rehabilitated it (1900/1904).

Art.21: the mapping theorem as stated depends on the Dirichlet principle and tacit boundary-regularity assumptions. Its proof was not rigorous by modern standards; complete proofs came from Osgood (1900), Koebe, Carathéodory, and Fejér–Riesz.

Art.21 implicitly requires the surfaces to be proper (not the whole plane) and bounded by curves. The normalization count (one interior point plus one boundary point, i.e. 3 real parameters) is correct.

results.what: Classification of isolated singularities of holomorphic functions (Art.13)
results.modern_name: Isolated singularities / Riemann removable singularity theorem

results.what: Minimization of Ω = ∫[(α_x−β_y)^2+(α_y+β_x)^2]dT over boundary-preserving variations; unique minimizer gives a harmonic real part (Arts.16–17)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Thomson, Dirichlet; named and used systematically by Riemann (1851, 1857)

results.what: Existence and uniqueness of a holomorphic correction on a surface made simply connected by cross-cuts, with periods across cuts (Art.18)
results.modern_name: Existence of harmonic/holomorphic functions with prescribed boundary data and periods (Hodge-type decomposition)

results.what: Conformal equivalence of simply connected plane surfaces, normalized by one interior and one boundary point (Art.21)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851); rigorous proofs by Osgood 1900, Koebe, Carathéodory 1912

results.what: Holomorphic functions viewed as conformal maps between surfaces spread over the plane (Art.15)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the table of contents of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation, copied by Weber. Every item (Dirichlet principle, cross-cuts, Riemann mapping theorem) is well known as Riemann's.

checkable.asserts: The integrand equals |grad a|^2+|grad b|^2 minus twice the Jacobian (result 0).
The Jacobian term is a divergence (null Lagrangian), so it contributes only boundary terms (result 0).
The Euler-Lagrange equation in a is -2*Laplace(a)=0, so the minimizer's real part is harmonic (result 0).
The integrand vanishes for a holomorphic function u+iv (Cauchy–Riemann; result 0).

transcription_corrections: Art.15: 'im Raume [?] der Ebene A' is doubtful; the dissertation reads 'einer über die Ebene A ausgebreiteten Fläche T', so probably 'über die Ebene A'.
Art.14: '[?]' after 'beliebigen' is probably superfluous: 'auf Punkte im Innern einer beliebigen ebenen Fläche'.
Art.20: 'enthielt' should grammatically be 'enthielten' (plural 'Bestimmungsweisen'); the manuscript may read so.
Art.18: the closing phrase is 'und letztere an den Querschnitten beiderseits gleich', referring to the variations (Änderungen) of ν, not to the integrals.
